admission.justification: Constrains future changes to task-doc source preparation, canonical source/copy rollback and the shared central publication boundary; it preserves the explicit rejected inverse, central-only and nested-success alternatives rather than presenting them as deferred work.

alternatives.option: One repository task-root file lock spans task_doc source read and preparation and is re-entered by the central publisher through validation, publication, refresh and rollback; a call-scoped marker refuses nested publication before writes.
alternatives.reason: The architect's L54-C05 task-document publication ruling and both amendments close the actual interval with the existing kernel primitive. Another thread/process waits and prepares after rollback; same-call nested publication is refused rather than falsely credited as a foreign success.

alternatives.option: Add a per-key inverse to undo the failed batch against the latest source generation.
alternatives.reason: The architect ruled that closing the interval makes whole-source snapshot restoration correct; a second inverse mechanism is not built for the same fact.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A production requirement demonstrably needs independently successful publication inside the rollback interval and the architect explicitly revises the serialization boundary.

alternatives.option: Take the task-root file lock only around the central transaction after task_doc has read and prepared its candidate.
alternatives.reason: The preparation-gap amendment identifies that a waiting question writer would retain the failing batch's source operand and refuse its exact CAS after rollback instead of preparing and publishing against the restored source.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The authoritative read/prepare boundary is changed by an approved design that still proves the waiting writer publishes from the restored source without implicit retries.

alternatives.option: Allow a successful same-thread publication inside copy refresh because the file lock is re-entrant.
alternatives.reason: Re-entrancy alone admits the review counterexample: snapshot rollback erases that nested success. The amended criterion distinguishes a real foreign thread/process from a nested publication and requires the latter to refuse before writing.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A real production path needs publication inside publication; the worker must stop and obtain an architect ruling before changing the active-marker refusal.

consequences: The sibling lock file is derived from the repository task root by kernel.file_lock.lock_path_for; the ordinary task_doc and central publisher share its same-thread re-entrant hold.

The central call-scoped active marker is reset in finally, including failures. Nested task_doc entry returns task-document-publication-in-progress; direct nested central publication raises its named task-document error before the publisher runs.
Whole-source snapshot rollback is retained. Other independently prepared topology, retirement and linkage callers keep exact CAS and clean refusal on a race, with no automatic retry.
The abstract own-document/copy-set guarantee of INV-J3PYB0 remains unchanged; its publication realization states this actual enforcement mechanism.
context: Failed task-document copy refresh restores pre-batch canonical source snapshots. Without exclusion, another successful question publication could be erased; taking exclusion only after task_doc prepares an edit also leaves the waiting writer with a stale exact-CAS operand.
